3 16-05-2024 Heard learned counsel for the appellant as well as the learned APP for the State.

2. This appeal has been directed against the judgment dated 11.07.2023 and its consequential order dated 18.07.2023 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-I, Bagaha, West Champaran, in S.T.No. 63 of 2022, CIS No. 27 of 2022, SL No.720 of 2022, arising out of Mahila P.S.Case No. 44 of 2020, whereby the appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code, and was awarded to undergo seven years R.I. with fine of Rs.10,000/-, and in default of payment of fine, the convict was also directed to further undergo S.I. for six months.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-I, Bagaha, West Champaran
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3. The learned counsel for the appellants, while Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4393 of 2023(3)
dt.16-05-2024 making prayer for bail after suspension of sentence, has submitted that even the victim did not support the occurrence.
She could not even identify the appellant, who was present in the dock at the time of recording of the deposition.
The appellant is in custody since the year 2021.

4. Considering the facts and circumstances as well as the fact that there is no likelihood of the appeal being taken up in the near future, during the pendency of the appeal, let the sentence of the appellant, named above, be suspended and he be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.

West Champaran in connection with S.T.No. 63 of 2022, arising out of Mahila P.S.Case No. 44 of 2020.
5.
